_meta.note: Every primitive carries source_basis, derived_claim, and not_source_claim. status: settled (directly cited authority), derived (architectural mapping from sources), synthesis (AXM-native, repo-evidence/analogy only — most guarded). No entry here is a benchmark or capability claim.

primitives.name: Black-letter AXM

source_basis.supports: definition of black-letter law as settled rule

primitives.derived_claim: AXM should start where the rule is settled, the record exists, and the answer is not allowed to drift.
not_source_claim: FRE 901 does not govern every AXM market.
This is an architectural mapping, not legal advice.
primitives.failure_mode: primitive becomes metaphor without source trail

primitives.name: The waterline

source_basis.supports: measured cheapest-clearing model per hidden-graded task, with UNMEASURED as a first-class answer
the 51 hidden-graded solve rows the routing rests on

primitives.derived_claim: Routing authority is the cheapest model measured to clear a task under hidden grading: settled work routes to the floor, residue is named and priced, and an unmeasured cell answers 'unmeasured', never a guess.
not_source_claim: The waterline is a routing metaphor, not hydrology.
The measured set is five tasks, not a leaderboard or a scale claim.
A cell with no evidence layer is unmeasured, not passing.
primitives.failure_mode: a cell is asserted routable with no evidence layer behind it
primitives.next_baseline: the almanac hidden-knot corpus (PR #49) adds tasks that test the residue axis beyond task02

primitives.name: Hidden grading

source_basis.supports: hidden_files / hidden_run_command inject the deciding tests only after the candidate is frozen

primitives.derived_claim: A capability measurement is valid only if the deciding tests were never visible to the solver; agentic solvers iterate any visible grader into a pass, which measures the pipe, not the model.
not_source_claim: Passing a visible test suite is not evidence of capability.
This does not claim the hidden tests are complete — only that they were unseen at solve time.
primitives.failure_mode: the answer key leaks into the solver's context and every cell 'passes'

primitives.name: Proof knot

source_basis.supports: the actual integrity / tamper-evidence guarantee (Merkle-tree hashing)
shard = signed knowledge artifact; any covered byte change flips the Merkle root
the 'knot record' naming only — a sealed unit of recorded fact

primitives.derived_claim: A proof knot is a sealed, independently verifiable unit of recorded fact: its integrity is checkable from the bytes alone, offline, with no trust in the producer.
not_source_claim: The quipu is an analogy for the name, not a technical specification.
The integrity guarantee comes from BLAKE3 Merkle + ML-DSA-44 in axm-genesis, not from the metaphor.
A signature proves integrity and publisher identity, not that the source content is true (AXM Genesis paper, section 9).
primitives.failure_mode: the knot metaphor is used to imply a guarantee the crypto does not actually provide

primitives.name: Frontier capture ledger

source_basis.supports: real-billed vs shadow-estimated cost rows that a capture ROI must distinguish
the 'LLM at compile time, SQL at query time' cost-shift: inference moves off the runtime path

primitives.derived_claim: Expensive frontier cognition is justified only when it is converted into reusable machinery (a grader, edge family, routing rule, or shard); the capture ledger records what was captured, what it cost, and when it breaks even against retired future frontier calls.
not_source_claim: No break-even is proven yet — this names the object PR #48 builds; it is captured-not-yet-amortized.
A routing demo is not a capture; capture requires a durable artifact plus a replay count.
This is not a benchmark claim.
primitives.failure_mode: frontier spend is called an 'investment' with no artifact and no measured amortization
primitives.next_baseline: PR #48 implements capture_ledger.schema.json + capture_roi.py with a worked task02 example

primitives.name: AXM provenance layer

source_basis.supports: section 8.3 — language models are compile-time extractors whose output can be reviewed, corrected, rejected, signed, and frozen; never runtime authority
section 0 provenance rule: primitive -> source_basis -> derived_claim -> testable schema -> verifier -> failure_mode -> next_baseline

primitives.derived_claim: Every AXM primitive must carry a source trail (source_basis), a stated synthesis (derived_claim), and explicit guards (not_source_claim), enforced by a verifier that rejects unsourced primitives — so persuasive prose cannot become fact by repetition.
not_source_claim: This layer proves attribution and separates fact from synthesis; it does not prove any sourced claim is correct.
The provenance ledger it draws on is itself model-authored synthesis, recorded as such (source axm_provenance_ledger, gpt-5.5-high).
primitives.failure_mode: a coined term circulates as settled fact with no source trail behind it

primitives.name: The AXM primitive ontology

source_basis.supports: the source map of AXM primitives (black-letter AXM, quipu, waterline, capture ledger, proof knot, terrain-divergence knot)
the Spectra runtime concept named in the ecosystem, born on gpt-4o

primitives.derived_claim: The AXM vocabulary is a starting ontology under active revision, not a fixed truth; each term earns its place only by carrying provenance.
not_source_claim: This ontology was authored with gpt-5.5-high (and 'Spectra' with gpt-4o); it is a starting ontology, not revealed truth (per the ledger's own section 0).
No primitive in this registry is a benchmark or capability claim.
Naming a primitive does not build it — several here are architectural intent (e.g. capture_ledger) pending implementation.
primitives.failure_mode: the model-generated vocabulary is mistaken for an established standard
